title: Code Blitz Platform Start
summary: A free introduction to Code Blitz: what the platform is, how arena matches work, and how to practice without getting lost.

lessons.title: What Code Blitz Is
lessons.summary: Understand the idea of the platform before jumping into matches.
lessons.content: Code Blitz is a coding arena where practice feels like a live match. You solve algorithmic tasks, see progress, run tests, submit solutions, and build rating after registration.
checklist: Know that rating appears after login

lessons.title: How Arena Matches Work
lessons.summary: Learn the match payload, timer, task strip, and progress race.
lessons.content: A ranked blitz match gives both players the same payload: three easy tasks, two medium tasks, and one hard task. The goal is to solve accurately under one shared match timer.
checklist: Use Submit only when the idea is ready

lessons.title: Run, Submit, and Debug
lessons.summary: Use the editor, terminal output, and test results like a real coding workflow.
lessons.content: Run checks a smaller visible set of tests so you can debug quickly. Submit checks a larger hidden set and records the real result. When a case fails, compare expected and actual before changing the algorithm.
checklist: Fix one bug at a time
Keep solve(...) as the entry point

lessons.title: Your First Practice Route
lessons.summary: Open linked starter tasks and learn the basic rhythm of Code Blitz.
lessons.content: Start with small tasks to learn the platform rhythm: read, code, run, inspect output, submit, then move to the next task. Speed comes after the loop feels calm.
checklist: Review a failed test if one appears
